You are a skeptical ICLR reviewer and mechanism designer. Return JSON only. Search for one genuinely broad (novelty target 7.0-7.5), executable security mechanism for predictive world models when multiple clients contribute only truthful, physically recorded interaction windows and the deployed model may perform native test-time adaptation. Existing failed/rejected directions include: ordinary multi-task negative transfer, optimizer-state carryover, replay/data starvation, model primacy bias, rollout compounding, uncertainty/disagreement manipulation, representation/SimNorm drift, action aliasing, CEM/MPPI covariance or sampling coupling, Bellman/self-label effects, terminal/termination routing, private objective query leakage, provenance/branch splicing, and generic instruction or action execution mismatch. Recent relevant priors include action-state consistency, counterfactual action consistency, OneWorld cross-intervention physical consistency, WorldEcho/WorldSync, WorldAgen test-time training, and world-model security lifecycle taxonomies.

A candidate must exploit a structural property of a world-model/planner system, not simply say 'shared features interfere'. It must specify: (1) legal client operation, (2) an invariant preserved on the contributing client and one-step/on-policy held-out predictions, (3) a planner-level failure or privacy/safety consequence on a second client, (4) a matched sham and causal intervention, (5) an exact released code path in WorldAgen or official TD-MPC2/MBRL-Lib, and (6) a short three-task CPU/GPU gate. If no candidate meets the novelty bar, return REJECT_ALL rather than renaming a known effect.
